newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close lower as sellers dominate.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close lower as sellers dominate.

text.p: Sell orders dominated dealings through the day to push the market to a lower close, traders said.
Lack of foreign institutional buyers, profit taking and concerns over the weak Tokyo bourse were cited as the chief reasons for the skid.
"We have been strong in the last two weeks. I think today is profit taking and forced selling," said one research chief.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks fell 9.34 points to 1,211.04. The Second Board index slumped 8.30 to 600.56.
"There were a lot of sell orders from many houses. A lot of people were taking profits," said a local brokerage dealer. "We are looking at 1,200 as the next market support."
Losers overwhelmed gainers 483 to 112 on total volume of 178.4 million.

"I think the market's consolidating. There's no good news to push higher," said Liew Yin Sze, chief economist at J.M. Sassoon. "I'm beginning to think most of the good news on the economy are already in share prices," he added.
Blue chip falls were led by United Engineers, UMW, Sime Darby and Hicom which fell between 25 and 70 cents.
